open: I want to be taken seriously, and I'm not shy about it.

open: All I want is a quiet, settled life.

hidden: Nobody knows how much I ache for a little peace.

I dream of a little cottage where nobody knocks.

open: I want someone to come home to.

I'd like someone to share the little things with.

I'd love someone to talk to over breakfast.
hidden: Nobody would guess how much I hate the empty house.
I act fine on my own, but I long for someone waiting up.

Privately, the loneliness gets heavier every winter.

I fill my evenings so I don't notice how alone I am.
I'd never admit how much I want someone to come home to.

open: I want a little adventure before it's too late.

I want to see what's past the hills.
I'd like a story worth telling my grandkids.
Give me somewhere new, and I'll go.
hidden: Nobody guesses how badly I want to throw it all in and go.
Under the routine, I'm dying for something to happen.
I'd never say it, but I dream of far-off places every night.

If they knew how restless I truly am, they'd be amazed.
I look at the road out of town more than I should.

open: I want to be recognized for what I do.

I want my name attached to something good.

I'd like my work to be noticed.

I want folk to know what I've done.
hidden: Nobody knows how much I crave a little praise.

Behind the humble face, I'm hungry to be seen.

I'd love someone to say they saw what I did.

open: I want to be needed. It makes me feel useful.

hidden: Nobody would guess how much I need to be needed.

Behind the busy hands, I'm afraid of being surplus.
Being needed is how I know I'm worth something.

open: I never want to worry about money again.
Enough put by for a rainy day. That's my dream.

I'd like to stop counting every coin.
I want a roof I know will stay over my head.
I'd like to stop worrying about next month.

hidden: Nobody knows how much money keeps me up at night.
I act carefree, but I'm terrified of going without.

I'd never say it, but being poor again is my biggest fear.
Behind the smile, I'm always one bad month from panic.
I lie awake doing sums nobody knows about.
I'll never feel safe until there's plenty put by.
I hide how frightened I am of going without.

open: I want to belong somewhere. Really belong.

I want to feel at home somewhere.
I'd like a place where people save me a seat.
Being part of a group means a lot to me.
hidden: Nobody would guess how much I want to fit in.

open: I want to get away from here someday.

hidden: Nobody knows how badly I want to leave this place.

I never mention it, but my mind is always somewhere else.
I've imagined leaving so many times it feels real.

open: I want to make my family proud.

hidden: Nobody would guess how much my family's approval still matters.

town.text: a place that is truly their own

open: A front door with my own name painted on it. That's the whole dream.
Rented rooms have had enough of my life.

hidden: Every lit window on the way home makes my chest tight.

There's a list in my drawer of what my own kitchen will hold.
On Sundays I walk past the cottages for sale, just to look.

town.text: to answer to nobody

open: Nobody telling me what to do. That's my idea of heaven.
My own hours, my own rules, my own mistakes.
Some morning soon I'll wake and decide the day entirely for myself.

Answering to nobody would suit me down to the ground.
hidden: Every order I take with a smile, I'm quietly counting the days.

What I dream of is one morning with nobody expecting anything.
Being told what to do grinds me down, and I hide it well.
There's a jar of coins under the floor for the day I walk away.

town.text: to be forgiven for something long past

open: Years ago I did something, and I'd give a lot to be forgiven for it.
There's one person whose pardon I'd walk a hundred miles for.

hidden: An old wrong of mine visits me most nights.

Under the cheerful face, I'm waiting on a forgiveness that may never come.

town.text: to be truly excellent at one thing

open: The best at my craft. Not good, the best.
One craft, done perfectly, is all the ambition I need.
My hands should know this work by heart someday.
Competent is not enough for me. Mastery is the goal.

Out loud I'd never claim it, but I mean to be the very best.

Being merely good feels like failing, to me.

town.text: to leave something behind that lasts

open: Something of mine should still be standing when I'm gone.
The town ought to be a little better for my having been here.

Fifty years from now, I hope my work still matters to someone.
Planting trees I'll never sit under seems a fine way to spend a life.
hidden: Being forgotten frightens me more than anything else does.
Quietly, I need some part of me to last.
What I'll leave behind is on my mind far more than anyone suspects.
Being remembered matters to me so much it embarrasses me.
Behind all the modesty, I want my life to have counted.

town.text: one friend who would stand by them through anything

open: One true friend. Just one would do.

Acquaintances I have plenty of. A real friend is rarer.
Who could I tell every silly secret to? I'd love to find out.
hidden: Lots of people know me, but none would come running if I called.
People with a best friend make me secretly envious.
What I long for is someone I could really confide in.
Everyone thinks I'm well liked. In truth there's nobody close.
Never once have I had a friend I could tell everything, and it shows.

town.text: to be rich enough to spoil the people they love

A fortune would suit me nicely. Enough to splash about.
Money to throw at good times, that's my dream.

Fine things, and the money to pay for them. Why not?
hidden: Dreams of riches keep me company most nights.
Content is how I look. Hungry is how I feel.

How much I want real money would shock my friends.
Under the shrug sits a great big appetite for wealth.

town.text: to be known far beyond their own street

People in faraway towns should know my name one day.

My name in print is a daydream I'd never confess.

town.text: to see the ocean at least once

Someday I'll stand on a beach and watch the waves come in.
Salt water on my toes, just once. That's all.

Behind my quiet face, I'm still furious.

town.text: to make peace with an old friend they fell out with

town.text: to pass on what they know before it's lost

town.text: to make one truly beautiful thing

Under the jokes, I just want someone to understand.

town.text: to finally beat their rival

Second to them for too long. That ends soon.

hidden: My rival is on my mind far more than is healthy.
Not caring is the act. Winning is the craving.

Beating them means everything to me, though I'd never admit it.

town.text: to keep the people they love safe

Strong enough to protect the ones I love. Nothing else matters as much.

If trouble comes, I'll be standing in front.

town.text: to go back to where they grew up

hidden: Homesick, after all these years. Still.

Missing where I came from is a secret ache.

town.text: a garden of their own to grow things in

A patch of earth to dig in is the whole dream.

Give me a garden and I'll be happy forever.
hidden: Seeds wait in a drawer for soil I don't have.
My hands in the earth is what I picture on bad days.

town.text: to perform in front of a crowd just once

open: Performing in front of an audience, just once.

hidden: Helpless is how I feel more often than anyone would guess.

Steering my own course is the dream I return to.

town.text: to make a real difference in someone's life

open: Making a difference to somebody. That's the goal.

Mattering to someone in a real way would be enough.
My life should help others somehow.
Making things better for someone is all I'm after.
hidden: My life not mattering is a worry I carry quietly.
When I hand someone a loaf, I'm really hoping it changes their day.
Just getting by is how it looks. Wanting to help is the truth.
Changing something is my secret wish.

town.text: to know what really happened

open: The truth about what happened. That's all I'm asking for.

hidden: The not-knowing eats at me.

Knowing is a need I keep to myself.

town.text: to laugh more and worry less

open: More laughter in my life. More silliness, too.

hidden: It's been ages since I truly laughed.

Content on the outside, grey on the inside.
Joy is a longing I don't share with anyone.

town.text: a second chance at something they once lost

open: A second chance. I'll do better this time.
One mess, long ago. I'd like another go.
Just one more chance would be enough.
Trying again, knowing what I know now, would be a gift.

hidden: Blowing my first chance is my deepest regret.
Trying again is a wish I'd give anything for.
Moving on is what I claim. Not true.
A do-over is my secret daydream.
That moment replays in my head a hundred times a week.

town.text: to rise up in the world

open: Higher in the world than I started. That's the plan.
Getting ahead, step by step, suits my patient nature.

hidden: How hard I'm working to climb would surprise people.

town.text: to be someone's first choice

open: Somebody's first choice. Just once.

hidden: An afterthought is what I've felt like most of my life.
Being chosen first is my private longing.
Not minding being second is the act. I mind.
Being overlooked cuts deeper than anyone knows.
Waiting to be chosen, and rarely chosen, is my lot.

town.text: to stop pretending to be someone they're not

open: No more pretending. Just me, as I am.
Dropping the act for good would be such a relief.
Being myself, openly, is the goal.

hidden: Pretending has worn me out.
The real me might not be liked, and that terrifies me.

Being myself is a longing I've never voiced.

town.text: a good name in the town

open: A good reputation, and people speaking well of me.
My name should mean honesty around here.
Known as someone decent. Surely that's not much?
A good name is worth more than gold to me.
Folk nodding when my name comes up. That's the goal.
hidden: What people say about me worries me constantly.
A single rumour could ruin my whole week.
Not caring is how I seem. My reputation matters terribly.
Being thought well of is a desperate wish of mine.
My ears prick up whenever my name is mentioned.

town.text: a shop of their own to run

open: My own shop someday. That's the plan.
A little shop with my name over the door.
My own boss, behind my own counter. Lovely.
Customers coming in to see me, by name.
A shop of my own, and it'll be the best in town.
hidden: The spot for my shop is already picked.
At night I sketch my shop's sign.
Working for others is fine, I say. My own place is the dream.
My own counter is the dream I keep secret.
Years of saving have gone toward my shop.

town.text: the schooling they never got

open: Learning properly. I missed out as a child.
Going back to school would be wonderful.
Education matters to me more than most things.
The books everyone talks about. I'd love to read them.
Understanding things I was never taught would change my life.
hidden: What I never learned makes me ashamed.
Late at night I teach myself.
Books don't interest me, I say. They do.
Feeling behind everyone else is a secret pain.
Library books get borrowed in someone else's name.

town.text: a dog to walk every morning

open: A dog. A loyal one.
A pet to come home to would be lovely.
A cat on my lap at night is the dream.
An animal to look after, that's what I'd like.
A faithful dog would suit me down to the ground.
hidden: Every dog in the street gets a pat from me.
Lonely enough to want a pet badly, if I'm honest.
Animals are a nuisance, I say. I long for one.
Puppies in the market make my resolve crumble every time.
There's a name picked out for a pet I don't have.

town.text: to see an old friend again

open: Seeing an old friend again would make my year.
Someone I lost touch with. I'd love to find them.
A reunion is what I'm hoping for.
Sitting and talking with someone from long ago would be wonderful.
Wherever they are, I'll find them, and we'll catch up.
hidden: An old friend is on my mind more than anyone knows.
Where they are now is a question I ask every day.
Moving on is what I claim. Missing them is the truth.
Their face still turns up in crowds, then turns out to be a stranger's.
Their last letter lives in my coat pocket.

town.text: to repay a kindness they never forgot

open: Someone helped me once, and I'd like to repay them.
A kindness I owe, and I mean to pay it back.
Someone saved me. Returning the favour is my aim.
Until I've repaid them, I won't rest.
Paying back a debt of kindness comes before anything else.
hidden: How much I owe someone weighs on me.
An unpaid kindness haunts me.
Independent is my reputation. Owing a great deal is my truth.
Repaying them is a need I never mention.
Their kindness comes to mind every single day.

town.text: to prove the doubters wrong

open: Proving everyone wrong about me is what drives me.
They said I couldn't. I'll show them.
The doubters will eat their words.
Their faces when I succeed. That's what I'm waiting for.
Spite is a fine fuel, and I've plenty.
hidden: Those old doubts still sting.
Every success of mine is aimed at them.
Carefree is the look. Fighting their words is the truth.
Proving them wrong is a need I'd never admit.
Their surprise when I make it is a picture I keep close.

town.text: to be the first to do something

open: First to do something. That's the ambition.
Going where nobody has gone before would be grand.
Being first is everything to me.
Something no one's tried yet. That's where I'm headed.
One day they'll say I did it first.
hidden: How badly I want to be a pioneer would surprise people.
Lying in bed, I invent firsts and give them my name.
Following is the act. Leading is the wish.
Being first means everything, though I hide it.
Plans for things nobody's done fill my notebooks.

town.text: to grow wise

open: Wise. Truly wise. That's the goal.
People coming to me for good counsel would be an honour.
Wisdom, if it can be learned, I'll learn it.
Understanding life deeply is my aim.
Growing wise with age seems the best kind of growing.
hidden: Foolish is how I feel most days.
When people quote some old sage, I wish it were me.
Knowing things is the act. Real wisdom is the hope.
People seeking my advice is a secret wish.
Old sayings get read in hope some will stick.

town.text: to finish what they started long ago

open: Something I started years ago deserves finishing.
A project left undone. I'm going to complete it.
Finishing it would lift a weight I've carried for years.
Seeing it done before I'm old would be enough.
That thing will be finished, I swear it.
hidden: The unfinished thing nags at me constantly.
It's on my mind every night.
Letting it go is the story. It isn't true.
Finishing it is a need I keep quiet.
It's waiting in a box under my bed.

town.text: to host a grand feast for the whole street

open: A grand feast for everyone I know. That's the dream.
A long table full of food and friends.
A party the whole street remembers would be wonderful.
Feeding everyone till they burst is my idea of joy.
A spread fit for royalty, laid on by me. Wouldn't that be grand?
hidden: The menu for my feast is already planned in my head.
Being the host everyone thanks on the doorstep would warm me for a year.
Modest on the outside, I long to throw a grand party.
A full table is a wish I keep to myself.
Recipes for my feast have been saved for years.

town.text: a clear conscience

open: A clear conscience, and a good night's sleep.
Living honestly, with nothing to regret.
A clean conscience matters to me more than money.
Anything I've done wrong, I want to set right.
No secrets weighing on me. That's the aim.
hidden: My conscience is heavier than anyone knows.
A small wrong keeps me awake.
At ease is how I look. Guilt follows me around.
Old mistakes knock at my thoughts whenever things go quiet.
Lists of things to set right fill my notebook.

town.text: a cause worth giving their life to

open: A cause to fight for. That's what I need.
Giving my life to something bigger than me would be worth it.
A purpose beyond myself would give my days a shape.
Joining a movement that matters would be grand.
Fighting for what's right is my calling.
hidden: Without a cause, I feel empty.
Something to believe in is my secret longing.
Settled is how I seem. Searching for meaning is how it is.
Needing a cause is something I never admit.
Reading about movements makes me wish I'd joined.

town.text: a business partner they can trust

open: A partner in business I can rely on.
Someone to build something with would be wonderful.
A trustworthy partner is what I need.
Someone to share the load. That's all.
Two heads are better than one, and I'd like a second.
hidden: Running things alone leaves me very lonely.
Someone to share decisions with is my secret wish.
Self-sufficient on the outside, exhausted inside.
Needing a partner is something I hide.
A few people have been sized up for the role, quietly.

town.text: one beautiful thing they don't need

open: One beautiful thing just for me.
A fine object I don't need. That's my wish.
Treating myself to something lovely would be wonderful.
Something extravagant, just once.
A bit of luxury. I've earned it.
hidden: Fine things in shop windows catch my eye every time.
Owning something beautiful is my secret longing.
Practical on the outside, dreaming of luxury inside.
Something lovely is a wish I keep quiet.
Exactly what I'd buy is already picked out.

town.text: to write a book

open: A book of my own, written by me.
My words in print. Imagine.
A book with my name on the spine is the dream.
Telling my story in pages would mean everything.
That book is getting finished, even if it takes me twenty years.
hidden: Every night I write.
Chapters hide in a drawer.
Not a writer, I say. I long to be one.
Being published is my secret wish.
My book on a shelf is a dream I return to.

town.text: to discover something nobody knew

open: Something new, discovered by me.
Finding something nobody's seen would be thrilling.
A discovery with my name on it.
Uncovering a secret of the world is my aim.
Turning over stones until I find something new. That suits me.
hidden: Every odd stone I pick up might be the great find. I check them all.
Clues get collected everywhere I go.
Ordinary is the act. Discovering something is the wish.
Explorers in old stories make me ache with envy.
Notes on things I've noticed fill a little book.

town.text: to make their corner of town a better place

open: This street deserves better, and I mean to help it get there.
Mended lamps, clear gutters, a few young trees. Not much to ask.
Neighbours who know each other's names again would make me happy.
Why shouldn't our corner be the nicest in town?
A tidy square with a bench for the old folk is my little project.
hidden: Sweeping the step, I'm really picturing the whole street made over.
Plans for the empty lot sit in my drawer, shown to no one.
Watching this place go shabby wounds me, though I joke about it.
If anyone knew how much I fuss over our corner, I'd blush.
At night I count the broken windows and imagine them mended.

town.text: to be left alone for once

open: Just leave me in peace, that's all.
A door that locks and nobody knocking. Lovely.
My business should stay my business.
Would one room nobody else walks into be too much?
Peace and privacy, that's my whole wish list.
hidden: Every knock at the door makes me want to hide under the table.
Constant company wears on me far more than I show.
Callers get a smile from me and a silent plea to leave.
Vanishing for a week without anyone fussing sounds like bliss.
Keeping my door open is a habit I've come to resent.

town.text: to keep a promise made long ago

open: A promise I made long ago is still waiting to be kept.
There's a vow I owe someone, and I'll see it through.
My word was given years back. It still stands.
However long it takes, that promise won't be broken.
Of all I'll ever do, keeping my word to them matters most.
hidden: That promise sits on my chest every single day.
Not a soul knows about the vow I'm still trying to honour.
Some nights I'm afraid I'll run out of time to keep my word.
Failing this one promise is something I couldn't forgive in myself.
Everything I save goes toward a promise nobody here knows about.

town.text: to make music well enough to play for others

open: Teach me a fiddle and I'll be happy for life.
Real music, from my own hands. That's the dream.
Playing a tune that makes people stop and listen. Imagine!
Singing in tune, out loud, for once. Could I?
An instrument, played properly, would mean the world.
hidden: Humming in private, I wish desperately I could really play.
There's an old instrument under my bed I'm too shy to touch.
When a band plays, I look away so nobody sees my face.
Practising scales when the house is empty is my quiet shame and joy.
Music moves me so much it frightens me a little.

town.text: to win a prize at the fair

open: First prize at the fair this year. Mark my words.
A ribbon, a rosette, a little cup. I'd treasure it.
This year my jam is going to beat everyone's.
My name on the winners' board would make my summer.
Just once, couldn't the blue ribbon come home with me?
hidden: The fair is just for fun, I tell people. I've been plotting for months.
Losing that prize again would hurt more than I'd ever admit.
A spot on my mantel is kept clear for a cup I haven't won.
It doesn't matter, I say. It matters terribly.
My entry has been tested forty times this summer, in secret.

town.text: to be thought clever

open: Thought clever, for once. That would be something.
The one with the smart answer, just occasionally.
Being thought bright would mean a lot to me.
Holding my own in clever conversation is my aim.
If someone said, now that's a sharp mind, I'd glow for a week.
hidden: The slowest one in the room is how I've always felt.
Witty remarks get practised alone, then vanish when it counts.
Being thought dim is my oldest, quietest fear.
When people explain things slowly to me, I want to sink through the floor.
The papers get read twice so I'll seem sharp at supper.

town.text: to finally say what they've never said

open: There's something I need to say to someone, and I will.
Getting something off my chest is long overdue.
The truth about one thing, told at last. That's my aim.
One honest conversation is all I'm after.
Quiet too long. Time to speak.
hidden: A sentence has been stuck in my throat for years.
The words get rehearsed every night and lost by morning.
If I said it, everything might change. That's what scares me.
There's a secret of the heart I've never told anyone.
Almost saying it, then talking about the weather, is my usual trick.

town.text: to make peace with the past and move on

open: Letting go of the past would free me.
Old hurts are heavy. I'd like to put them down.
Moving on is my aim this year.
Forgive and forget, properly. Could I manage it?
Ready to put the old business behind me, I think.
hidden: Old hurts still wake me at night, years later.
Moved on, I say. My chest says otherwise.
The same old quarrels replay in my head, over and over.
There's a weight I can't seem to set down, however hard I try.
Being haunted by things long finished has worn me thin.

town.text: everyone at home getting along

open: Peace at home, everyone getting on. That's the dream.
A house without arguments would be bliss.
One supper with no quarrels at the table. Is that so much?
Everyone under this roof being friends would make me so happy.
Harmony at home is what I'm working toward.
hidden: Every slammed door at home goes through me like a knife.
Playing peacemaker is how I cope with the bickering.
How much the squabbles hurt me, nobody has guessed.
A single quiet, friendly evening in would be worth a great deal.
Lying awake, I listen for raised voices.

town.text: to do one truly brave deed

open: Something heroic, just once in my life.
Saving the day when it really counts would be grand.
One brave deed people remember. That's my wish.
If there's ever a fire or a flood, let me be the one who helps.
Somebody's hero. Wouldn't that be something?
hidden: Daydreams of rescues fill more of my hours than I'd admit.
When the moment comes, what if I don't step up?
Part of me waits for an emergency just to prove myself.
Wanting to be brave in a big way is a wish I've never shared.
Ordinary days feel like rehearsals for a moment that never comes.

town.text: to be welcomed in the best houses

open: Invitations to the finest gatherings. That's my aim.
Moving in good society would suit me nicely.
Dinner at the grand houses, at least once.
Rubbing shoulders with important folk sounds like fun.
One day an invitation with gold edges will arrive for me.
hidden: How fine people talk gets studied and practised alone.
Being looked down on by the gentry stings deeply.
A good coat hangs ready for an invitation that never comes.
High society doesn't interest me, I claim. It does, enormously.
Being announced at the door is a little dream of mine.

town.text: for someone to look after them for once

open: Someone looking after me, for a change.
A cup of tea brought to me, unasked. Heaven.

Being fussed over for once would be nice.
Tucked in at night, just once, by someone else.
hidden: Looking after everyone, I'm the one nobody notices is tired.
If someone asked how I was and meant it, I might cry.
Being strong for everyone has left me starving for care.
Being fussed over is something I've almost forgotten the feel of.
On my worst days I pretend I'm fine, because nobody would come anyway.

town.text: to understand who they really are

open: Understanding myself better is the real work.

Surprising myself less often would be nice.
hidden: Often I feel like a stranger in my own head.
Not knowing what I really want frightens me.

Lost inside myself is how I'd describe it, if anyone asked.
Some mornings the person in the mirror is a stranger.

town.text: for life to surprise them again

open: Let life surprise me again, please.

Amazed by something, just once more.

hidden: Every day feels the same, and it's slowly crushing me.
Bored enough to weep, and nobody notices.

town.text: a life worth telling stories about

open: A life worth telling stories about. That's the aim.

hidden: My life feels too dull to be remembered.

town.text: for things to stay exactly as they are

open: Everything just as it is, forever. That's my wish.

hidden: Each change, however small, sends me quietly reeling.

town.text: to be trusted completely

open: Trusted completely, that's what matters to me.

hidden: Doubted so often, it still stings.

When someone checks my work, I feel small for days.
Being distrusted once left a mark I still feel.

town.text: to be proud of themselves for once

Something that makes me hold my head up. That's all.
Pleased with myself? That would be new.
hidden: Never once have I felt proud of anything I've done.

Looking in the mirror and feeling glad would be a miracle.
How disappointed I am in myself stays hidden.
Something worth being proud of keeps not arriving.

town.text: land of their own to work

open: A bit of land to call my own.

hidden: Maps of farms for sale are folded in my drawer.
Stuck indoors, I dream of fields.

My own ground is a longing I never mention.
Since I was young I've been saving for land.

town.text: a say in how things are run

open: A say in how things are run. That's my aim.
My opinion should count around here.
Influence, real influence, would suit me well.
The council, someday. Why not me?
Having a voice in big decisions would suit me.
hidden: Being ignored frustrates me deeply.
Shaping how this town works is my secret ambition.
Politics bore me, I claim. They don't.
Wanting power, even a little, is something I'd never confess.
Plans for the town that nobody asked for fill my notebook.

town.text: to speak another language fluently

open: Another language, spoken properly. That's my goal.
Chatting with travellers in their own tongue would be marvellous.
Fluency in something foreign is my aim.
Books in other languages, read without a dictionary.
Answering someone in their own language, to their surprise. That's the dream.
hidden: Foreign words get practised alone, the books hidden away.
Being the clever one who speaks three tongues is my daydream.
Learning languages is a wish nobody suspects.
When travellers pass, I long to talk with them.
For years I've taught myself, very badly.

town.text: to be surrounded by beautiful things

open: Beauty around me every day would make me a better person.
Flowers on the table and a view from the window.
Somewhere lovely to live would mean everything.
Beautiful things, beautiful places. That's my wish.
My home should be a pleasure to look at.
hidden: Ugly rooms make me low in a way I can't explain to anyone.
A single beautiful room would be worth a great deal.
Pretty things get collected and hidden away.
A sunset moves me more than anyone knows.
A life full of loveliness is my quiet dream.

town.text: to make it entirely on their own

open: Making it on my own, with nobody's help. That's the goal.
Built it all myself. That's what I want to say.
Self-made, start to finish.
Handouts? No thank you. I'll earn it.
My success will be mine and mine alone.
hidden: Accepting help is something I hate.
Owing my success to anyone would shame me.
Proving I can do it alone is a need I hide.
Being dependent is a fear I never voice.
Every kindness offered feels like a threat, privately.

town.text: to find the work they were meant to do

open: My calling, the work I'm meant for. That's what I'm looking for.
There's something I'm supposed to be doing. I'll find it.
A trade that feels like it fits is my wish.
Waking up glad to get to work would be wonderful.
Drifting from job to job has to stop.
hidden: Every job I've had feels like wearing someone else's coat.
What if I never find what I'm meant to do?
How lost I feel at work, nobody guesses.
People who love their work make me terribly envious.
Knowing what I'm for would settle something deep down.

town.text: more hours in the day

open: More time. There's never enough.
A few more hours in the day would make me happy.
Time for myself, without guilt. Is there such a thing?
A day with nothing scheduled. Imagine!
More time with the people I love. That's my wish.
hidden: Always rushing, and it's wearing me thin.
Life slips past while I'm busy.
The hours I've lost, I mourn quietly.
If I could slow the days down, I'd do it in a heartbeat.
Minutes get counted like coins, and I'm always short.

town.text: to be a good example to the young

open: A good example for the young ones. That's my aim.
Children looking up to me for good reasons. That would be something.
Being a good influence matters to me.
Showing the next lot how it's done is my job.
Someone worth copying. That's who I'd like to be.
hidden: Being a poor example is a fear I carry.
The young admiring me is a secret wish.
Some of my habits shame me in front of children.
When a child copies something I do, my heart leaps.
Better behaviour comes out of me when the little ones are watching.

town.text: to build something with their own hands

open: Something built with my own two hands.
A boat, a house, a bridge. Something solid.
Something that stands for years, made by me.
Building it myself is the dream.
Pointing at something solid and saying I made that. Imagine!
hidden: Plans for a little cabin are sketched in my notebook.
Timber for a project I've never started is stacked in my shed.
Being the one who built something lasting is a quiet dream.
Everything I've ever made has fallen apart, and it haunts me.
Watching builders makes me itch to join them.

town.text: for one particular person to notice them

open: One particular person noticing me. That's all.
Seen by them, really seen. That's my wish.
Being noticed by them would be enough.
They should remember my name.
One glance from them would make my week.
hidden: Out of my way I go, just to cross their path.
Who I'm hoping will notice me is my secret.
My best coat comes out on days I might see them.
Being overlooked by them hurts more than anything.
Them turning and smiling at me is my daydream.

town.text: an honest living with nothing to hide

open: An honest living, nothing fancy.
Fair pay for fair work. That's all I ask.
A job I'm not ashamed of would be wonderful.
Plain honest work is my aim.
Earning my bread straight would let me sleep sound.
hidden: Some of my work isn't as honest as I'd like.
How I've earned money before shames me.
A clean job, one I could describe to anyone, is my private hope.
Cutting corners for a wage is something I'd give a lot to stop.
Work I can talk about openly is my dream.

town.text: to become a kinder person

open: Kinder. Truly kinder. That's the goal.
Gentler with people, that's what I'm working on.
Being a better person is my aim.
Thinking before I snap would be a start.
Kindness is what I'm practising.
hidden: How sharp I can be shames me.
Unkind things I've said keep me awake.
How hard I try to be gentle, nobody sees.
People calling me kind would be a dream.
What if I never soften?

town.text: to get their affairs in order

open: My affairs in order. That's the plan.
Bills paid, papers sorted, debts settled.
Everything tidy and settled would be such a relief.
Putting my life in order is my aim.
Knowing where everything stands would let me breathe.
hidden: My affairs are a mess, and it frightens me.
Unpaid bills keep me awake.
How chaotic my papers are, nobody knows.
An orderly life feels as far off as the moon.
Anyone seeing the state of my accounts is a dread of mine.

town.text: to know where their people came from

open: Where my people came from. That's what I'd love to know.
Tracing my roots back is my project.
Knowing my history would help me know myself.
The village my grandparents left. I'd love to find it.
My roots matter to me, and I'll find them.
hidden: Rootless, and it's lonely.
Old town ledgers draw me in, and I never say why.
Old records get searched in secret.
Finding people I'm related to would mean the world.
Not knowing where I come from leaves a hole.

town.text: a challenge worth rising to

open: A real challenge, something hard. Bring it on.
Give me a mountain to climb, so to speak.
Tested properly, for once. That would be grand.
Easy is boring. Something difficult, please.
A worthy challenge is my wish.
hidden: Everything feels too easy, and I'm restless.
How bored I am, nobody knows.
Being pushed to my limits is a secret longing.
Growing old untested scares me more than failing.
A task worthy of all I've got is what I dream of.

town.text: to complete a collection

open: My collection, finished at last. That's the goal.
Just a few more pieces and it'll be complete.
The full set would be a triumph.
Completing it would be the proudest day of my life.
One day my collection will be the finest around.
hidden: How much I spend on my collection, nobody knows.
The missing pieces keep me awake.
Someone else getting the last one would crush me.
A bit obsessed, if I'm honest.
The day the shelf is full is a day I dream of.

town.text: to be admitted as a full member of their trade

open: A full member of my trade. That's the goal.

Joining the guild properly would be grand.
Recognised as a true craftsperson, at last.
My name on the roll of masters. Imagine.
hidden: How many times I've been turned down, nobody knows.
My masterpiece gets practised in secret.

Wearing the guild's badge is my daydream.

town.text: to stop working and enjoy their later years

open: Retiring somewhere quiet is the plan.

hidden: Worn out, and dreaming of stopping.

town.text: to hear someone say sorry

open: Someone saying sorry to me. That's what I'm owed.
An apology is all I'm after.
Them admitting what they did would help.
One word from them would mean a lot.
I'm owed an apology, and I'd like it.
hidden: Still waiting, after all this time.
