The hurt replays, and so does their imagined apology.
Maybe they'll never say it. That thought keeps me up.
The silence from them hurts most.

town.text: to step out of someone else's shadow

open: Out of someone's shadow at last. That's the goal.
Known for myself, not as someone's relative.
My own name, my own achievements.
People seeing me, not who I'm compared to.
Standing on my own would show them who I really am.
hidden: Being compared to someone all my life is exhausting.
How much I resent the comparisons, nobody knows.
Being seen for myself, just once, would be a gift.
Always being in their shadow is what I expect, sadly.
My own light is what I dream of.

town.text: a fair chance, just once

open: Just one honest shot, with nobody stacking the deck against me.
Competing on level ground. That's all.
A fair shot would be plenty.
The same opportunities as everyone else would do.
Give me a fair go and I'll prove myself.
hidden: Never having a fair chance burns.
How many doors have closed on me, nobody knows.
Being judged on merit is my secret hope.
Never getting a fair shot is what I'm braced for.
A level playing field is my dream.

town.text: to trust someone again

open: Trusting someone again. That's my aim.
After everything, believing in people would be a gift.
Letting my guard down, for once.
Faith in someone. I'd love to have it.
Opening up again is what I'm working toward.
hidden: Hurt too badly to trust easily.
How lonely suspicion makes me, nobody knows.
Trusting again would heal something old.
Staying closed up forever is what I'm afraid of.
Someone I can rely on is my dream.

town.text: to restore something old to its former glory

open: Something old, restored to its glory. That's the dream.
An old house, a boat, a clock. I'd love to bring it back.
Restoring it is my project.
Seeing it shine like new would be wonderful.
One day it'll look as it did.
hidden: How much I've spent on old things, nobody knows.
Seeing it restored is my dream.
Leaving it half done is what keeps me up at night.
People admiring what I've brought back would be lovely.
Talking to the old thing as I work is a habit nobody sees.

town.text: for luck to finally turn their way

open: My luck turning at last. That's my wish.
Things going my way, just once.
A bit of good fortune wouldn't go amiss.
Surely I'm due some luck?
One lucky break is all I need.
hidden: Unlucky is how I feel, always.
Charms go in my pocket, just in case.
My luck never changing is what I quietly expect.
A sudden windfall is my daydream.
Every setback makes me feel cursed.

town.text: to recover something precious that was lost

open: Something precious that was lost. I want it back.
An heirloom, found again. That's my wish.
Recovering it is my aim.
It belongs where it was, and I'll put it there.
Someday, somewhere, I'll track it down.
hidden: Missing it is a constant ache.
Markets and shops get searched for it.
Gone forever? I can't bear to think so.
Holding it again would mean more than any treasure.
Its loss still hurts, years later.

town.text: to be asked along, not as an afterthought

open: Invited along. That's all.
Asked, not added on. That's my wish.
Being included would make my whole week.
People thinking of me first would be lovely.
An invitation is all I want.
hidden: How left out I feel, nobody knows.
Gatherings get mentioned to me after they've happened.
Being an afterthought forever is my dread.
Being wanted at the table is my dream.
Not minding being left out is a pretence.

seen: gives advice nobody asked for
offers a fix before the problem is fully told
can't hear a complaint without suggesting a remedy
has an opinion on how everyone should run things
tells others what to do, unprompted
owned: I know, I know, nobody asked for my advice.
I hand out advice like bread, whether anyone's hungry or not.
I should just listen, but the fix jumps out of my mouth first.
Yes, I'm doing it again. Telling you how to fix it.
kind: I'm just being helpful.
If I see a better way, it seems unkind to keep quiet.
I'd want someone to tell me, so I tell them.
I only speak up because I care how it turns out.

seen: finishes other people's sentences
grabs the last word before the speaker gets there
guesses the end of a thought out loud
completes whatever someone else started to say
supplies the missing word before it's needed
owned: Sorry, I did it again. Go on, finish your own sentence.
I have a terrible habit of finishing everyone's thoughts for them.
My mouth runs ahead of yours, I know.
I keep stealing the ends of people's sentences.
kind: I'm just following along closely.
It shows I understand exactly what you mean.
I'm only trying to help the conversation along.
We're on the same wavelength, that's all.

seen: hums tunelessly while working
whistles the same few bars over chores
fills quiet rooms with half-remembered tunes
sings snatches of songs without noticing
keeps a melody going under every task
owned: I know I hum. Everyone tells me.
I don't even notice the tune until someone points it out.
Yes, that's me humming again. I can't help it.
My hands work better when there's a song going.
kind: A little music makes any job lighter.
It's a happy noise. Where's the harm?
Humming keeps me steady, that's all.
Silence feels heavy, so I fill it gently.

seen: swears in strange and inventive combinations
curses like a poet with a grudge
invents oaths nobody has heard before
turns a stubbed toe into a colourful speech
has a remarkable vocabulary for stubborn jars
owned: My language gets colourful. I won't pretend otherwise.
I swear too much, but at least I'm original about it.
Sorry for the language. It just comes out.
I've been told my cursing could strip paint.
kind: A good oath clears the air.
Better to curse at the thing than at a person.
It's honest. I say exactly how I feel.
If I'm going to swear, I'll make it worth hearing.

seen: repeats the same pet phrase in every conversation
has one saying that answers everything
leans on a favourite expression until it wears thin
says the same catchphrase at every turn
brings back one stock line again and again
owned: I know I say it all the time. It's my phrase.
People tease me for my favourite saying, and fair enough.
I've worn that expression smooth, haven't I?
There I go with my old line again.
kind: It's a good phrase. Why change it?
People know it's me when they hear it.
It says what I mean better than anything new.
Familiar words are comforting, for me and everyone.

seen: remembers every birthday and anniversary
keeps track of everyone's special days
never forgets a name day or a wedding date
marks other people's milestones without being reminded
turns up with a token on exactly the right day
owned: I keep a calendar of everyone's days. It's a bit much.
Yes, I remembered. I always remember.
I collect dates the way some collect pretty stones.
It's odd, but I can't forget a birthday if I try.
kind: Everyone deserves to feel remembered.
It costs me nothing to say happy birthday.
Small days matter more than people admit.
I just like seeing someone's face light up.

seen: changes the subject when things get serious
steers away whenever talk turns heavy
finds something else to discuss the moment feelings surface
brightly asks about the weather mid-confession
slides out of hard conversations with a new topic
owned: I know I dodge. Hard talk makes me itch.
Did I just change the subject again? I did.
I bolt from serious talk. It's an old habit.
Whenever it gets heavy, I reach for another topic.
kind: Not everything needs to be picked apart.
I'm keeping things light for everyone's sake.
Some things are better left unsaid for now.
There's a time for serious talk, and it isn't now.

seen: laughs off every compliment
waves away praise as if swatting a fly
answers kind words with a joke
insists any success was pure luck
can't accept a thank-you without arguing
owned: I'm hopeless at taking a compliment, I know.
Praise makes me squirm, so I joke it away.
Someone says something nice and I immediately brush it off.
I never know what to do with kind words.
kind: I'm just being modest.
It really wasn't anything special.
I don't like a fuss made over me.
Plenty of people did more than I did.

seen: interrupts others mid-sentence
talks over whoever is speaking
cuts across others mid-thought
can't wait a turn in conversation
jumps in the moment a thought arrives
owned: I interrupt. It's rude and I keep doing it.
Sorry, sorry. You were talking. Go on.
My thoughts won't wait their turn.
I've been told I talk over people, and they're right.
kind: I just get excited about what we're saying.
If I wait, I'll lose the thought.
It's lively talk, not rudeness.
Conversation should move, not crawl.

seen: keeps careful score of favours given and owed
remembers whose turn it is to host
tallies every kindness in a private ledger
notices when a favour isn't returned
counts who visited whom last
owned: I keep score. I wish I didn't.
I know it's petty, but I remember who owes what.
There's a ledger in my head and it's always open.
Yes, I counted. I always count.
kind: I'm just making sure things are fair.
Someone has to keep track.
Fair is fair. I give as good as I get.
I only notice because I care about balance.

seen: fidgets with whatever is within reach
twists a ring or button when nervous
can't keep both hands still
rolls crumbs or threads between restless fingers
picks at a sleeve while listening
owned: My hands never stop. I've given up trying.
I fidget. Ignore it, please.
Give me something to hold or I'll unravel your tablecloth.
I know I'm twitchy. It's how I'm built.
kind: It helps me think.
Busy hands, steady head.
I'm not nervous, just full of energy.
Keeping my fingers moving keeps me calm.

seen: stands a little too close in conversation
leans in until there's no room left
closes the distance whenever talking
doesn't notice when someone steps back
talks nearly nose to nose
owned: I stand too close. Push me back if you need to.
People keep stepping away from me, and I keep following.
I've no sense of distance at all, I'm told.
Am I in your space? I usually am.
kind: I just want to hear properly.
Closeness is friendly where I come from.
I like to really be with whoever I'm talking to.
Distance feels cold to me.

seen: drums fingers on the table
taps a foot through every conversation
beats out a rhythm on any flat surface
keeps time on the nearest tabletop
raps knuckles on wood while waiting
owned: Sorry, the tapping. I'll stop. I won't, but I'll try.
I always drum on something. It drives people mad.
My foot has a mind of its own.
Someone once sat on my hands to stop the tapping.
kind: It's just a little rhythm.
I think in beats.
It keeps the waiting from dragging.
Some people knit. I drum.

seen: tidies other people's things without asking
straightens anything left crooked
reorganises a friend's shelves while visiting
folds and stacks whatever is lying about
can't leave a mess alone, even someone else's
owned: I straighten everything. I know it's not my house.
My hands tidy before my head can stop them.
Yes, I moved your things. Sorry. They looked untidy.
I can't sit in a messy room. I've tried.
kind: I'm only helping out.
A tidy room is a gift to everyone.
I just like things where they belong.
Order makes everyone calmer, not just me.

seen: arrives early to everything
is waiting before the doors even open
turns up well ahead of the hour
treats being on time as being late
gets restless when others aren't early too
owned: I'm always first. I can't help it.
On time feels late to me, so I come early.
I'd rather wait an hour than be a minute behind.
Yes, I've been here a while. I always am.
kind: Being early is a kind of respect.
Someone has to be ready.
I like to settle in before things start.
Punctuality is simple courtesy.

seen: over-explains simple things
answers a yes-or-no question with a whole story
adds three reasons where one would do
explains the explanation
can't give a short answer
owned: I over-explain. I'm doing it right now.
Short version? I don't have one.
I know, too much detail. It's how my mouth works.
I give the whole map when someone asks for the next street.
kind: I just want to be understood.
Better too clear than misunderstood.
Details matter, and I don't want to skip any.
I'd hate for anyone to get the wrong idea.

seen: feeds everyone who walks through the door
presses food on guests until they beg off
always has something warm on the stove
asks if you've eaten before saying hello
sends visitors home with leftovers
owned: I feed people. It's a compulsion.
You'll leave here full whether you like it or not.
I know I push food on everyone. Have another.
My answer to everything is a plate of something.
kind: Nobody should go hungry under my roof.
Food is how I say I care.
A full belly fixes half the world's troubles.
I just like seeing people eat well.

seen: runs late to everything
arrives breathless with a fresh excuse
treats a set hour as a rough suggestion
turns up after the start, every time
loses track of the hour completely
owned: I'm late. I'm always late. I'm sorry.
Time slips through my fingers, it always has.
People tell me the wrong hour on purpose now.
I swear I left in plenty of time.
kind: The best things happen when they happen.
Something always comes up on the way.
I got caught up helping someone.
I'm never late for anything that truly matters.

seen: can't keep a secret past supper
passes along things told in confidence
lets slip what was meant to stay private
repeats confidences to the next listener
treats a secret as something to share
owned: Don't tell me anything you want kept. I'm a sieve.
I mean to keep secrets. They just leak out.
I know, I promised. It slipped.
Secrets burn a hole in me until I share them.
kind: I only told one person, and they won't say anything.
It wasn't really a secret, was it?
I thought everyone already knew.
Sharing news brings people together.

seen: knows everyone's business before they do
keeps a running map of who's feuding with whom
always has the latest about the neighbours
hears about every quarrel within a day
tracks the comings and goings of the whole street
owned: I know everything about everyone. It's a gift and a curse.
If something happens on this street, I hear about it.
I'm nosy. I've made my peace with it.
Ask me anything about anyone. I probably know.
kind: I'm not nosy, I just pay attention.
Somebody has to know what's going on.
People tell me things. I don't go looking.
Knowing the neighbours keeps us all safer.

seen: drops to a whisper to share the latest news
starts every story with a glance over the shoulder
lowers the voice for the juicy part
delivers news in a conspiratorial hush
beckons people closer before sharing anything good
owned: I whisper the good bits. I know it's theatrical.
Lean in. Yes, I'm doing my secret voice again.
I can't share news at a normal volume, apparently.
Everything sounds better in a whisper, I find.
kind: I'm only being discreet.
Not everyone needs to hear this.
Keeping it quiet is the respectful thing.
I lower my voice so nobody gets embarrassed.

seen: watches the street from behind a curtain
notes every visitor on the lane and the hour
keeps an eye on who comes and goes
twitches the curtain at every passing footstep
knows which doors opened late last night
owned: Yes, I watch the street. Someone has to.
I'm a curtain-twitcher and proud of it.
I see who comes and goes. I can't help looking.
Nothing gets past my window, I'm afraid.
kind: I'm keeping watch for everyone's sake.
I just like to see the world going by.
It's neighbourly to notice.
If something happened, you'd be glad I saw.

seen: retells everyone's private stories at dinner
spreads a good tale faster than it happened
embroiders the stories passed along
turns a friend's mishap into the evening's entertainment
adds a little colour to every rumour shared
owned: I improve a story every time I tell it.
I know, it wasn't my story to tell.
By the third telling it's a much better tale.
I can't resist a good story, even someone else's.
kind: A story's meant to be told.
I only make it more fun to hear.
Everyone was laughing, even the one it was about.
People like hearing about each other.

seen: tries to pair off every unattached friend
speculates about who's courting whom
plots introductions between likely couples
can't see two people chatting without guessing at romance
keeps a mental list of matches to make
owned: I'm a terrible matchmaker and I'll never stop.
I see two lonely people and start plotting.
Yes, I seated you together on purpose.
I know, I meddle in other people's hearts.
kind: I just want everyone to be happy.
Some people need a little push.
Love deserves a helping hand.
I'm good at seeing who fits together.

seen: cracks a joke when things get tense
answers bad news with a quip
breaks every awkward silence with a wisecrack
laughs loudest in the worst moments
turns a quarrel into a punchline
owned: When it gets tense, I get funny. I know.
I joke when I'm scared. Always have.
Sorry. Bad timing for a joke. It's what I do.
My first answer to trouble is a punchline.
kind: Someone has to lighten the mood.
Laughter helps more than worry.
If we can laugh, we can get through it.
I'm just keeping spirits up.

seen: scrubs the floor whenever upset
starts cleaning in the middle of an argument
buries feelings under a pile of chores
polishes things hard when angry
finds urgent work to do whenever feelings come up
owned: When I'm upset, the whole house gets cleaned.
I scrub instead of talking. I'm aware.
If you see me polishing, something's wrong.
I'd rather beat a rug than say how I feel.
kind: Work settles the mind.
I'm just getting things done.
Feelings can wait. The chores can't.
Being useful helps more than moping.

seen: turns every personal question back on the asker
answers a question with a question
keeps the spotlight firmly on others
deflects curiosity by asking about the other person
shares almost nothing about personal matters
owned: I'd rather hear about you. I always would.
I know I never talk about myself.
You asked me something and I turned it around, didn't I?
My life isn't interesting. Tell me yours.
kind: Other people are more interesting than me.
I'm a listener, not a talker.
I just care about what's going on with you.
There's nothing much to tell, honestly.

seen: says everything is fine when it clearly isn't
insists on being fine through gritted teeth
smiles and says it's nothing
waves off concern with a quick all right
hides a bad day behind a cheerful answer
owned: I say I'm fine. I'm rarely fine.
Fine is my favourite lie.
I know I hide it when things are bad.
I'll say it's nothing even when it's something.
kind: I don't want to burden anyone.
Other people have bigger problems.
I'll manage. I always do.
No sense making a fuss over little things.

seen: apologises before saying anything at all
says sorry for taking up room
begins every request with an apology
apologises to furniture after bumping into it
says sorry three times in one breath
owned: Sorry. I know. I apologise too much. Sorry.
I say sorry like other people say hello.
I've apologised to a door before. Twice.
I can't ask for anything without apologising first.
kind: It's just good manners.
I'd rather apologise than offend.
Saying sorry smooths things over.
A little courtesy goes a long way.

seen: tops every story with a better one
has always done it bigger or worse
can't let anyone else's tale stand alone
follows good news with even grander news
turns every shared hardship into a contest
owned: I do one-up people. I hear it as I'm saying it.
Your story reminds me of mine, which was, well, bigger.
I know, I always have to top it.
I can't let a good story go unmatched.
kind: I'm just relating, showing I understand.
I'm sharing, not competing.
It's how conversation works, trading stories.
I only mention it so you feel less alone.

seen: wanders off on tangents mid-story
loses the thread three times per tale
starts one story and finishes another
follows every side path in a conversation
rambles until the point is long forgotten
owned: Where was I? I always lose my place.
I go off on tangents. Bring me back.
My stories have more detours than a country road.
I never get to the point. I just enjoy the trip.
kind: The side roads are the best part.
Everything's connected if you think about it.
A good story takes its time.
I'm just giving you the full picture.

seen: corrects small details in other people's stories
stops a tale to fix a date or a name
can't let a minor mistake pass
points out the error nobody else cared about
insists on the exact figure every time
owned: I correct people. It's a sickness.
I know it doesn't matter. It was Tuesday, though.
I can't let a wrong detail slide.
Yes, I'm being pedantic. I'm aware.
kind: Getting it right matters to me.
I'd want to be corrected, so I correct.
Facts are facts, whatever the mood.
I'm saving you from repeating a mistake.

seen: says the harsh thing out loud
delivers honest opinions without softening them
answers a fishing question with the plain truth
tells people the very thing nobody wants to hear
never pads a hard truth with kindness
owned: I'm blunt. Ask me only if you want the truth.
I know I could say it more gently. I don't.
Tact was never my strong suit.
I say what I think, and sometimes it stings.
kind: I'm just being honest.
At least you know where you stand with me.
Sugarcoating is a kind of lying.
The truth helps more than flattery ever could.

seen: flatters anyone who might be useful
lays compliments on thick
praises everything a little too warmly
says exactly what each listener hopes to hear
has a kind word ready for anyone of rank
owned: I butter people up. I'm good at it.
I know my compliments come a bit thick.
Yes, I flatter. It opens doors.
I praise people a little more than they've earned.
kind: I'm only being kind.
What's wrong with making people feel good?
I see the best in everyone.
A pleasant word sweetens any meeting.

seen: talks to animals and objects as if they answer
chats to the kettle while waiting
scolds tools that misbehave
names household things and speaks to them
carries on full conversations with the cat
owned: I talk to things. They're good listeners.
Yes, I named the broom. Don't judge me.
I chat with the cat more than with people.
I know it's odd that I argue with the door.
kind: Everything deserves a little kindness.
It keeps me company when I'm alone.
Saying things aloud helps me think.
Who's to say they don't hear?

seen: takes in every stray, animal or person
brings home whoever looks lost
always has a lodger nobody expected
finds room at the table for one more waif
adopts lost causes without a second thought
owned: I collect strays. Animals, people, whatever needs a home.
I know, another one. I couldn't leave them.
My door is a little too open, I'm told.
Every lost creature seems to find me.
kind: Everyone needs somewhere to land.
I couldn't walk past and do nothing.
There's always room for one more.
They'd have done the same for me.

seen: lends things out and never asks for them back
gives away belongings at the first hint of need
has borrowed books scattered across town
hands a cloak to anyone shivering
never keeps track of what was loaned
owned: Half my things live at other people's houses.
I lend everything. I never get it back.
I know, I gave it away again.
If you need it, take it. I mean that too much.
kind: Things are for using, not hoarding.
Someone needed it more than me.
It'll come back to me some other way.
Sharing is what neighbours do.

seen: brings a small gift to every visit
never arrives empty-handed
picks up little tokens for friends on errands
presses trinkets into people's hands
leaves small surprises on doorsteps
owned: I can't visit without bringing something. I just can't.
Yes, another little thing. I saw it and thought of you.
My pockets are always full of small presents.
I know, I don't need to bring anything. I always do.
kind: A little token says you were thought of.
It's how I was raised.
Small surprises brighten a dull day.
I just like giving more than getting.

seen: paces the room while thinking
can't hold a serious talk sitting down
wears a track in the floor when worried
walks in circles while working out a problem
gets up and moves the moment an idea takes hold
owned: I pace. I think with my feet.
Sitting still makes my head go blank.
I know I'm wearing out your floor.
I need to walk to get my thoughts in a line.
kind: Moving helps me think straight.
Sitting still is wasted time.
It's just nervous energy finding a way out.
My best ideas come on my feet.

seen: makes lists for everything
writes out a plan for a simple afternoon
crosses items off with visible satisfaction
keeps a list of the lists
won't start a task without writing it down first
owned: I make lists. Then I make lists about my lists.
If it isn't written down, I can't rest.
I know it's excessive. I love crossing things off.
There's a list for that. There's always a list.
kind: Lists keep me from forgetting what matters.
Planning saves everyone trouble later.
A written plan is a calm mind.
I'm just organised, that's all.

seen: checks the locks twice before leaving
goes back to make sure the fire is out
reads a letter three times before sending it
asks if everything is packed, again
can't trust a door is shut without trying it
owned: I've checked it twice. I'll check it again.
I know the door's locked. I still have to look.
I check everything more than I need to.
Leaving the house takes me a while.
kind: Better safe than sorry.
It only takes a moment to be sure.
One of us has to be careful.
I sleep better knowing it's done right.

seen: imagines the worst outcome out loud
lists everything that could go wrong
predicts disaster from every grey sky
turns a late arrival into a catastrophe
has a dark forecast for every plan
owned: I always expect the worst. It rarely comes.
I know, I'm catastrophising again.
My mind runs straight to disaster.
Give me a plan and I'll find ten ways it fails.
kind: I'm just being prepared.
If you expect the worst, you're never caught out.
Someone has to think ahead.
Worry is just love looking forward.

seen: fusses over everyone's health
insists on a scarf at the first chill
notices every cough and prescribes a remedy
asks if you've slept enough
wraps others in blankets unasked
owned: I fuss. I know I fuss.
Every sniffle around me gets a remedy.
Yes, I brought you soup again. You sounded hoarse.
I worry about everyone's health more than my own.
kind: Someone has to look after you.
A little care now saves a lot of trouble.
I just want everyone well.
Better a scarf than a fever.

seen: goes quiet in a crowd
sits at the edge of a lively table
listens far more than speaks in company
speaks once an evening, and only briefly
fades into the background at gatherings
owned: Put me in a crowd and I go silent.
I'm better one on one, I know.
I listen at parties. Talking is harder.
People forget I'm there, and that's my fault.
kind: I learn more by listening.
Not everyone needs to fill the air.
I'm happy just watching.
I speak when I have something worth saying.

seen: writes down odd facts in a little notebook
jots notes in the middle of conversations
copies out interesting words to keep
carries something to write on everywhere
records the day's small details every night
owned: I write everything down. Everything.
Don't mind me, just making a note.
My notebooks would fill a whole shelf.
I can't hear a good line without writing it.
kind: Memory fades, but ink lasts.
I just don't want to lose anything.
Little details become treasures later.
Writing helps me understand things.

seen: asks question after question
wants to know how everything works
follows every answer with another why
quizzes strangers about their trades
can't let a puzzle rest
owned: I ask too many questions. I know.
Sorry, just one more question. Maybe two.
My curiosity wears people out.
I need to know how things work, always.
kind: How else does anyone learn?
Curiosity keeps the mind young.
I'm genuinely interested in people.
Asking shows I care what you think.

seen: never admits to being wrong
argues long after the point is lost
rewrites the story so the mistake was someone else's
won't apologise for a wrong turn
digs in harder when proven mistaken
owned: I hate being wrong. I'll argue rather than admit it.
I know I dig in. I just can't back down.
Saying I was wrong sticks in my throat.
Yes, I'm stubborn. Annoyingly so.
kind: I just believe in what I say.
I stand by my word.
Someone has to hold firm.
I'm not stubborn, I'm sure of myself.

seen: haggles over everything, even gifts
can't buy a loaf without bargaining
treats every price as an opening offer
argues the cost of everything at the market
enjoys the bargain more than the purchase
owned: I haggle. I'd haggle with my own shadow.
Paying the first price feels like losing.
I know the stallholders groan when I come.
Bargaining is my favourite sport.
kind: Everyone expects a little haggling.
I'm just being sensible with what I have.
Waste not, want not.
Nobody respects someone who pays whatever's asked.

seen: jokes about personal failings before anyone else can
puts self down for a laugh
mocks own looks and luck with a grin
beats everyone to the punchline about own mistakes
laughs at own clumsiness loudly and first
owned: I make fun of myself first. Saves everyone the trouble.
I know I'm always the butt of my own jokes.
If anyone's going to laugh at me, it'll be me.
Self-mockery is my oldest armour.
kind: I don't take myself too seriously.
It's just humour, not a confession.
Laughing at yourself keeps you humble.
It puts people at ease.

seen: can't resist a terrible pun
groans at own wordplay before anyone else does
twists any phrase into a play on words
keeps a stock of awful jokes
waits for the groan after every joke
owned: I make puns. I'm not sorry.
Yes, that was a pun. There'll be more.
My jokes are bad and I love them.
I hear a pun and it has to come out.
kind: A groan is still a laugh.
Words are toys, and I like to play.
Someone has to keep things silly.
Bad jokes are good for the soul.

seen: sighs loudly until someone asks what's wrong
huffs and groans at every small setback
makes sure displeasure is heard
lets out long sighs across quiet rooms
mutters complaints just loud enough to catch
owned: I sigh a lot. Loudly. I'm aware.
I know I'm being dramatic. Let me be.
Yes, that sigh was meant for you to hear.
I huff when I want someone to ask.
kind: I'm only letting off a little steam.
It's not about anyone. I'm just tired.
Better a sigh than a shout.
Sometimes a sound says it all.

seen: makes a grand entrance everywhere
announces arrival to the whole room
sweeps in as if expected by everyone
pauses in doorways to be noticed
turns heads on purpose when arriving
owned: I like an entrance. I'll admit it.
If I come in quietly, something's wrong.
Yes, I paused at the door. On purpose.
I know I make a production of arriving.
kind: People like a bit of spectacle.
Life's too short to slip in unnoticed.
I'm just glad to see everyone.
Arriving should feel like an occasion.

seen: brings up the same old triumph
steers talk back to a single proud moment
retells a past success at every gathering
keeps polishing one long-ago victory
mentions the old achievement within the hour
owned: Did I mention that time? I always do.
I know, you've heard about my glory day.
I lean on one good memory a bit hard.
That story's worn thin, but I still love telling it.
kind: It was a proud day, and I earned it.
Good memories deserve airing.
It reminds me what I'm capable of.
People enjoy hearing about it, I think.

seen: keeps every letter and dried flower
saves ribbons and scraps for no clear reason
can't throw away anything with a memory attached
has drawers full of mementos
treasures small things others would discard
owned: I keep everything. Letters, buttons, all of it.
My drawers are a museum of small things.
I know it's clutter. It's precious clutter.
I can't part with anything someone gave me.
kind: Every little thing holds a memory.
You never know when you'll want it.
Throwing it away feels like forgetting.
These are pieces of my life.

seen: bites nails when nervous
chews the inside of a cheek while thinking
worries a lip between teeth
gnaws at a thumbnail during bad news
picks at cuticles under the table
owned: I bite my nails. My hands give me away.
I know, I'm chewing my lip again.
Whenever I'm worried, my fingers end up in my mouth.
There's not a nail left on me. Nerves.
kind: It's just a habit, nothing more.
Everyone has some little tic.
I'm thinking, not fretting.
It helps me concentrate.

seen: touches your arm while talking
rests a hand on a shoulder mid-sentence
pats hands to make a point
reaches out to touch whoever is speaking
squeezes a wrist when saying something kind
owned: I'm a toucher. I can't talk without reaching out.
Sorry, my hands find people's shoulders.
I know not everyone likes a pat on the arm.
I touch your sleeve when I mean something.
kind: A touch says what words can't.
It's warmth, nothing more.
I just want people to feel close.
Contact makes a conversation real.

seen: forgets to eat when absorbed in work
works straight through meals
notices hunger only after dark
lets a plate go cold beside the work
loses the whole day to one task
owned: I forget to eat. Then I'm a bear by evening.
Once I'm into something, meals don't exist.
I know, my food's gone cold again.
Someone has to put bread in my hand or I won't stop.
kind: When the work's flowing, you don't stop it.
I'll eat when it's done.
Hunger can wait. Ideas can't.
I just get lost in what I love.

seen: volunteers for everything
raises a hand before the request is finished
takes on every task nobody else wants
signs up and then signs up again
can't hear a call for help without offering
owned: I volunteer for everything. Then I'm drowning.
My hand goes up before my head catches up.
I know I've said yes to too much again.
If something needs doing, I'm somehow doing it.
kind: If I don't, who will?
Many hands make light work.
I like being useful.
It's nice to be needed.

seen: does impressions of everyone in town
mimics voices to tell a story
copies other people's walks for a laugh
slips into accents mid-tale
plays every character in an anecdote
owned: I do voices. I can't tell a story without them.
Yes, that was supposed to be you.
I know my impressions aren't always kind.
Give me a story and I'll act out every part.
kind: It's all in good fun.
Imitation is the sincerest flattery.
Stories need a bit of theatre.
People love seeing themselves played back.

seen: answers everything with an old proverb
has a saying for every situation
quotes folk wisdom at the slightest excuse
offers a proverb in place of comfort
drops a homespun maxim into every talk
owned: I've a saying for everything. Drives people mad.
Yes, another proverb. They're always true, though.
I know I talk like an old almanac.
My head is a jar of old sayings.
kind: Old words carry old wisdom.
Proverbs last because they're right.
My elders taught me well.
Why say it new when it's been said best?

seen: carries a pocketful of string, buttons and odd useful bits
always has whatever you need tucked in a pocket somewhere
produces a spare needle or a bit of twine at the drop of a hat
rattles faintly from all the oddments carried about
empties a pocket onto the table and finds three things nobody expected
owned: My pockets are a junk drawer with legs.
I carry half my house around with me, and I know it.
Somewhere on me there's a button, a nail and a boiled sweet.
I've given up pretending my pockets are tidy.
kind: You'd be amazed how often someone needs a bit of string.
I'm just ready for whatever the day throws at me.
Being prepared isn't clutter, it's sense.
Somebody always needs something, and I've usually got it.

seen: counts things under their breath without noticing
mutters numbers while stacking, sorting or climbing stairs
keeps a running count of steps, coins or loaves, half aloud
can be heard tallying something in a quiet room
loses the thread of talk the moment there's something to count
owned: I count everything. Stairs, spoons, you name it.
If I'm murmuring, I'm probably counting something.
I can't carry a basket of anything without numbering it.
Sorry, I was on forty-two. Where was I?
kind: Counting keeps me from losing track, that's all.
Numbers settle my mind. Nothing odd about it.
It's how I make sure nothing goes missing.
Plenty of careful folk count. I just do it out loud.

seen: opens every conversation with the weather
has an opinion on the clouds before saying good morning
reports on last night's rain to anyone who'll listen
can predict a downpour and will tell you so
treats a change in the wind as real news
owned: I can't help it, the weather is always my first topic.
I'll tell you about the sky before I tell you my name.
Rain, sun, frost, I've got something to say about all of it.
Yes, I'm talking about the weather again.
kind: The weather affects everyone. It's polite to mention it.
It's an easy way in. Everybody has a view on rain.
Somebody has to notice what the sky is up to.
Talking about the weather is how strangers become neighbours.

seen: talks with both hands flying
draws shapes in the air to explain anything
can't tell a story without acting half of it out
knocks over a cup now and then mid-explanation
goes quiet the moment their hands are full
owned: Tie my hands and I'd be speechless.
I talk with my hands. Stand back a bit.
Half of what I say is in the waving.
I've sent more than one mug flying making a point.
kind: It helps people picture what I mean.
I'm expressive, that's all. Words aren't always enough.
A story told with stiff arms is a dull story.
Folk follow me better when they can see it.

seen: always has their sleeves rolled up, ready for work
looks set to pitch in the moment they walk through a door
starts clearing plates before anyone asks
is first to grab the other end of anything heavy
seems uneasy standing about with nothing to do
owned: My sleeves are up before I know what the job is.
I can't watch somebody work without joining in.
Idle hands make me fidgety, so I find a task.
Show me a mess and I'm already halfway into it.
kind: Many hands make light work. I'm just one of the hands.
Why stand about when there's something to be done?
It would feel rude to watch and not help.
I'm happiest when I'm useful. That's not a fault.

seen: always has a book tucked under one arm
reads a page or two in any spare minute
is found in corners with a book propped on their knee
marks the place with a finger when someone says hello
brings a book to places nobody else would
owned: I never go anywhere without something to read.
If there's a queue, I've got a chapter to get through.
I'm that person reading at the back of every gathering.
Leave me waiting and I'll hardly notice. I'll have my book.
kind: Reading beats staring at the wall.
I'm not unsociable. I just hate wasting a spare moment.
A book is good company when the room isn't.
There's always time for one more page.

seen: always takes the seat facing the door
glances up every time someone comes in
picks a spot with a wall at their back
knows exactly who has arrived and who has left
keeps half an eye on the entrance through any conversation
owned: I always sit where I can see the door.
Nobody walks in without me clocking them.
Put me with my back to a room and I'm useless.
I can't settle until I've got the doorway in view.
kind: I like to see who's coming, that's all.
It's just the best seat. Good view of everything.
Somebody ought to keep an eye out.
I'm aware of my surroundings. Most people aren't.

seen: saves every jar, scrap and length of ribbon
keeps old buttons in a tin, just in case
won't let anything be thrown out that might still be useful
rescues things from the rubbish pile with obvious delight
has a cupboard nobody dares open
owned: I can't throw anything away. It might come in handy.
My shelves are full of things I'm saving for later.
Every scrap gets a second life in my hands, eventually.
I've a drawer of string too short to use. I keep it anyway.
kind: Waste not, want not. That's all it is.
You'll thank me when you need a jar.
Throwing good things away seems wrong to me.
I'm thrifty, not a hoarder. There's a difference.

seen: has a nickname for everyone within a day of meeting them
rarely calls anyone by their real name
hands out pet names to strangers and friends alike
renames the regulars after their habits
makes a nickname stick whether you like it or not
owned: I can't help giving everyone a nickname.
Once I've named you, that's your name around here.
I forget proper names but never a nickname I've made.
Half the town answers to something I called them once.
kind: A nickname means I like you.
It's friendly. It makes people feel part of things.
Proper names are so stiff. This is warmer.
Nobody's ever complained. Not to me, anyway.

seen: speaks with old-fashioned courtesy to everybody
uses full names and proper titles, never shortcuts
says good day and kindly in a way few still do
phrases a simple request like a formal letter
stays polite and correct even when teased for it
owned: I'm formal, I know. It's how I was raised.
I can't bring myself to call people by nicknames.
My manners are a bit stiff for this town, I suspect.
Even asking for the salt, I sound like a solicitor.
kind: Good manners never go out of style.
Courtesy is a sign of respect, nothing more.
I'd rather be too proper than careless.
Folk could do with a little more politeness.

seen: drops lines from old books and songs into everyday talk
has a quotation ready for every occasion
answers small questions with a verse
credits a long-dead writer for half their opinions
starts sentences with as somebody once wrote
owned: I quote things constantly. Someone always said it better.
There's a line from a book for everything, and I know most of them.
I answer in other people's words more than my own.
Yes, I'm quoting again. Bear with me.
kind: Why reinvent what's already been said perfectly?
It's a way of sharing what I love.
A good line deserves to be passed on.
People like a bit of poetry in their day, surely.

seen: can't walk past a wobbly table without fixing it
tightens loose hinges in other people's houses
carries a small tool or two everywhere
notices a squeaky door before anyone else hears it
is found on their knees mending something that wasn't theirs
owned: If something's broken, I have to fix it. Right now.
I've mended things in houses I was only visiting.
A rattle or a squeak and I'm off looking for a tool.
I can't sit at a wonky table. I just can't.
kind: It only takes a minute, so why not?
Broken things bother me. I'm doing everyone a favour.
It's just handy to know how things work.
Nobody minds getting something fixed for free.

seen: knows the price of everything and what it cost last year
can tell you where to buy it cheaper
remarks on prices the way others remark on the weather
keeps a sharp mental ledger of every market stall
sighs at every price as if personally wounded
owned: I know what everything costs, down to the penny.
Ask me the price of eggs anywhere in town.
I can't buy anything without comparing it in my head.
I remember when bread was half this price, and I'll say so.
kind: Somebody has to keep an eye on prices.
It's just being careful with money.
Folk get fleeced because they don't pay attention.
Knowing the going rate is common sense.

seen: walks everywhere, however far
turns down every offer of a ride
knows every shortcut and back lane in town
turns up a little windswept and very cheerful
measures distances in how long they take on foot
owned: I walk everywhere. Always have.
Offer me a lift and I'll say thanks, but no.
I know this town by its footpaths.
A good walk clears my head better than anything.
kind: Walking keeps me sharp.
You see more on foot. You miss everything otherwise.
Why pay to get somewhere my own legs can take me?
I like the time to think on the way.

seen: mentions having been up since dawn
has done half a day's work before most folk stir
flags by evening and says so cheerfully
talks about sunrises like other people talk about parties
is quietly smug about early mornings
owned: I'm up before the birds and I'll tell you all about it.
By the time you're awake, I've been at it for hours.
I'm useless after supper, but dawn belongs to me.
I do love telling people what time I got up.
kind: The best part of the day is gone by breakfast.
Early hours get things done. That's all.
I just like the quiet before everyone else starts.
Somebody has to be up to see the day in.

seen: always has soil on their cuffs from the garden
turns any chat toward seedlings and slugs
presses cuttings on anyone who admires a plant
reports on the beans like other folk report on family
can name every weed in a crack in the road
owned: Ask about my garden and you'll be here a while.
I've got earth under my nails more often than not.
Every visitor goes home with a cutting, like it or not.
My tomatoes get more of my attention than my friends do.
kind: Growing things is good for the soul.
Everyone's interested in a garden, deep down.
I just like sharing what's doing well.
It's a fine way to spend an hour, talking plants.

seen: knits or whittles through every conversation
always has a bit of handwork going in their lap
keeps their hands busy while listening closely
finishes a sock or a spoon in the time others take to chat
looks up from the needles only for the good parts
owned: I'm always making something while I talk.
My hands need a job, even when the rest of me is resting.
I can listen perfectly well with a half-done scarf in my lap.
Give me an evening's chat and I'll give you a finished mitten.
kind: It's not rude. I'm paying attention, truly.
Why waste the time? Talking and making go together.
It keeps me calm and the family warm.
Idle hands bother me, that's all.

seen: reads every sign and notice aloud while walking past
can't pass a posted notice without stopping
narrates the shopfronts on any stroll
quotes the price boards back to whoever's nearby
knows what every placard in town says
owned: I read every sign out loud. I can't seem to stop.
If it's written down, I'll say it as I pass.
Walking with me is like walking with a town crier.
I stop at every notice board, I'm afraid.
kind: I'm just interested in what's going on.
Somebody might miss something important.
It's how I keep up with the town.
Reading aloud helps me remember.

seen: uses your name in nearly every sentence
says a new acquaintance's name back three times
drops first names into talk like a seasoning
makes everyone feel addressed personally
never seems to forget a name once heard
owned: I say people's names a lot. It's how I keep them.
If I've just met you, expect to hear your name plenty.
I repeat names until they stick. Sorry if it's odd.
I'll use your name more than your own family does.
kind: Folk like hearing their own name.
It shows I'm paying attention to them.
It's respectful, remembering who you're talking to.
It helps a stranger feel known.

seen: takes a long pause before answering anything
lets a question hang while thinking it through
answers slowly, as if weighing every word
makes quick talkers wonder if they were heard
says little, but rarely needs to take it back
owned: I think before I speak. It takes a while.
Give me a moment. I'm getting the words right.
My pauses make people nervous. I'm only thinking.
I'd rather be slow than sorry.
kind: Better a slow answer than a wrong one.
Considered speech is a dying art.
I'm careful with words. They matter.
People should pause more, honestly.

seen: puts the kettle on at the first sign of trouble
answers bad news by fetching cups
seems to believe a hot drink fixes nearly everything
has a pot brewing before a visitor's coat is off
offers a warm drink in place of advice
owned: Something's wrong? I'll put the kettle on.
My answer to every crisis is a hot cup of something.
I make a drink before I make sense of anything.
I've poured more cups in hard times than I can count.
kind: Nobody thinks straight on an empty cup.
A warm drink is a kindness. It says I'm here.
It gives everyone a moment to breathe.
It's just what you do when someone's upset.

seen: tips their hat or nods to everyone they pass
greets passers-by with a little bow of the head
acknowledges every soul on the street, known or not
keeps up small courtesies most folk have dropped
nods to the cart drivers and the street sweepers alike
owned: I nod to everyone. Habit of a lifetime.
I can't pass a soul without some kind of greeting.
Strangers get a nod from me whether they want one or not.
My hat sees more lifting than wearing, some days.
kind: It costs nothing to acknowledge a person.
A greeting can turn someone's day around.
It's only manners, the way things ought to be.
Everybody deserves to be noticed.

seen: is always dressed for weather that never comes
carries a cloak or umbrella on cloudless days
has an extra layer for everyone, just in case
checks the sky before leaving and again on arrival
is quietly vindicated about once a month
owned: I always bring something for the rain. Always.
I'm the one with a spare scarf you didn't think you'd need.
Clear skies don't fool me for a minute.
I'd rather carry it all day than get caught once.
kind: You'll be glad of me when it pours.
It's sensible, not fussy.
Weather turns. I just don't get caught out.
Being ready is better than being wet.

seen: knows the history of every building in town
points out where the old mill or the old inn used to stand
dates any family back three generations on request
corrects newcomers on the proper name of a street
turns a simple stroll into a local history lesson
owned: Ask me about any house on this street and I'll tell you who built it.
I carry the old town around in my head.
Every corner here reminds me of something that happened.
I'm a walking record of who lived where.
kind: Somebody ought to remember how things were.
People like knowing the story of a place.
Forget the past and you lose half the town.
It's not lecturing. It's sharing.

seen: makes up little rhymes about whatever's happening
turns chores into songs with silly verses
can rhyme anyone's name with something ridiculous
leaves a ditty behind like other folk leave a smell of baking
groans at their own rhymes and keeps making them
owned: I make up rhymes all day. My poor friends.
Give me a word and I'll find something daft to rhyme it with.
Half my chores get done to a made-up tune.
I can't stop the verses coming, honestly.
kind: A bit of nonsense makes a hard day lighter.
Kids love it, and so does everyone, secretly.
It's harmless fun. Life's too short to be serious.
Rhymes help me remember things.

seen: remembers exactly how everyone takes their drink
has your usual ready before you've ordered
recalls that you hate onions from one meal years ago
knows everyone's favourite seat and saves it
stores little likes and dislikes like treasure
owned: I remember how everyone likes things. It's my small gift.
Tell me once you like it sweet and I'll never forget.
I keep a list in my head of what everyone prefers.
I know your usual better than you do.
kind: It's just paying attention.
Small things matter to people.
It makes folk feel cared for.
Anyone could do it if they listened.

seen: draws a little map for anyone who asks directions
can't give directions without sketching on something
turns a napkin into a chart of the neighbourhood
adds landmarks nobody else would think of
insists you'll get lost without the drawing
owned: Ask me the way and I'll draw you a map.
I can't explain a route in words. I need a scrap of paper.
My maps have little trees and everything.
I've drawn the way to the market a hundred times.
kind: A picture is clearer than any directions.
I don't want anyone wandering about lost.
It's quicker in the end, believe me.
People keep them. They must find them useful.

seen: nods along to every sentence
murmurs mm and yes throughout any story
agrees with a nod before the point is made
makes speakers feel heard, if not always understood
keeps nodding even when lost
owned: I nod a lot. Sometimes I don't even know I'm doing it.
I'm always going mm-hm, mm-hm while people talk.
My head's bobbing before you've finished the sentence.
I nod along even when I've lost the thread, I admit.
kind: It shows I'm listening.
Folk talk more freely when you encourage them.
I'm being supportive, that's all.
Better a nod than a blank face.

seen: waves at everyone, including people they don't know
waves from across the square with both arms
gets waved back at out of sheer surprise
greets a passing cart like an old friend
is spotted by the waving long before the face
owned: I wave at everyone. Some of them even wave back.
I've waved at strangers thinking they were friends. Often.
If I can see you, I'm waving.
My arm gets more exercise than my legs some days.
kind: A wave is free and it cheers people up.
Better to wave at a stranger than ignore a friend.
It's just friendly. What's wrong with friendly?
Everyone looks happier after a wave.

seen: wears the same coat every single day
is recognised from a distance by one familiar jacket
has mended the same sleeves more than once
hasn't changed their look in years
would be hard to picture in anything else
owned: I've worn this coat for years and I'm not stopping.
Folk would walk past me in anything else.
I find something I like and I stick to it.
This jacket has been patched more times than I can say.
kind: If it isn't broken, why replace it?
Good things last if you look after them.
I don't have time to fuss over clothes.
It's comfortable. That's all that matters.

seen: sweeps the front step every morning without fail
keeps the doorway spotless whatever the season
is out with a broom at first light
tuts at leaves blown onto the step
nods hello over the bristles to every passer-by
owned: I sweep my step every morning. Rain or shine.
The day doesn't start until the doorstep's clean.
I've worn out more brooms than I can count.
People set their clocks by my sweeping.
kind: A clean step says the household is in order.
It's a good way to greet the street.
Somebody has to keep the place decent.
It's routine, and routine keeps me right.

seen: saves crusts for the birds and pigeons
is followed by sparrows on most walks
carries crumbs in a twist of paper
knows the birds on their street by sight
pauses mid-errand to scatter a handful of seed
owned: The birds know me better than half the neighbours.
I never leave the house without crumbs.
I've names for some of the pigeons, if I'm honest.
A few crusts and I've got company for the morning.
kind: They've got to eat too.
It's a small kindness. Where's the harm?
Feeding birds is good for the heart.
They'd only go to waste otherwise.

seen: always has a worn deck of cards on hand
challenges anyone sitting idle to a quick game
shuffles absently while talking
knows a card trick for every occasion
keeps an old tally of games won, going back years
owned: I carry a deck of cards everywhere. Fancy a game?
Sit still too long and I'll deal you in.
My hands shuffle when they've nothing else to do.
I know more card games than I know people.
kind: Cards pass the time and bring folk together.
It's friendly competition, nothing more.
Nobody minds a game when they're waiting.
Keeps the mind sharp, a good game.

seen: knocks on wood after every hopeful remark
won't walk under a ladder for any money
has a little charm or lucky token about them
throws salt over a shoulder after spilling it
takes the same route to anything that matters
owned: I knock on wood. Every time. Don't laugh.
I've a lucky coin and I'd be lost without it.
I won't tempt fate. I've seen what happens.
Call me silly, but I'm not stepping under that ladder.
kind: A little caution never sank anyone.
It doesn't hurt, so why not?
Old habits exist for a reason.
Everyone has a little luck ritual. I'm just honest about mine.

seen: carries a huge ring of keys that jingles with every step
is heard coming long before being seen
seems to hold a key to half the buildings in town
sorts through a dozen keys before finding the right one
gets asked to open things simply for having the keys
owned: I've got keys to more doors than I can remember.
You'll always hear me coming. It's the keys.
I couldn't tell you what half of these open.
People trust me with their spare keys. I collect them.
kind: Being trusted with a key is an honour.
Somebody has to be able to get in.
It's handy, being the one with access.
Nothing odd about being prepared.

seen: says goodbye three times before actually leaving
starts a new story at the door with a coat on
lingers in the doorway long after announcing an exit
turns a farewell into another half hour
remembers one more thing just as the door closes
owned: My goodbyes take longer than my visits.
I always think of one more thing on the doorstep.
I mean to leave. I really do. Then I keep talking.
Put my coat on and that's when the best stories come out.
kind: Rushing off seems so cold.
Goodbyes matter. You never know.
I'm just enjoying the company.
The best talk happens on the way out.

seen: slips away from gatherings without saying goodbye
is there one minute and gone the next
leaves a party before anyone notices they're missing
avoids farewells with a quiet nod from the doorway
is found to have gone home only when someone looks
owned: I slip out without a word. Goodbyes aren't for me.
By the time you notice I've left, I'm home in my slippers.
I hate the fuss of leaving, so I just go.
I'm a master of the quiet exit.
kind: Why interrupt everyone's fun?
Nobody wants a fuss over one person leaving.
It's polite, really. Less disruption.
I said goodbye in my head.

seen: has a voice that carries across any room
is heard clearly from the far end of the street
makes a whisper sound like an announcement
turns heads by simply saying hello
can't share a secret without the whole room knowing
owned: I've a loud voice. I'm told I could call cattle home.
My whispering is everyone else's talking.
You'll never mistake me in a crowd. You'll hear me first.
I try to keep it down. It never lasts.
kind: At least everyone can hear me.
I speak clearly. Folk mumble too much.
There's nothing wrong with a strong voice.
It comes in handy in a noisy room.

seen: is always dressed as if for a special occasion
turns up to ordinary errands in their best
never seems to own anything casual
keeps a sharp crease in every garment
makes everyone else feel slightly underdressed
owned: I dress up for the market. I can't help it.
